scientificConclusion: V79 supports the user's core contextual hypothesis: a fixed route condition does not carry the same historical reliability across all pregame competitive-strength regimes. The effect is clearest in General V16+V68, where selected-stronger was 91-59 (60.67%), peers were 29-27 (51.79%), and selected-weaker was 8-9 (47.06%); strength gap also separated General wins from losses in the same adverse direction across all three seasons. A+ behaves differently and remains extremely strong when its selected team is pregame stronger. Premium-A does not show a useful team-strength-gap effect and should retain its separate HR-risk investigation. Crucially, V79 rejects the simple rule 'stronger opponent means bet the opponent': every broad predeclared stronger-opponent flip context was approximately coin-flip or negative. The more plausible use of dynamic strength is route-aware qualification / NO PLAY, especially around competitive parity, not automatic side reversal. Because the specific cell patterns were observed on the same retrospective window, no live context gate is promoted by V79; any next gate must be frozen and validated on fresh data.
